# Retail CoD 1.1d dedicated server item notifies and pickup log lines under the
# --save-pickup client.
# map mp_carentan, g_gametype probe_pickup (whose main() calls
# maps\mp\gametypes\dm::main()), joined allies, dedicated 1, sv_maxclients 8,
# sv_pure 0, stock scr_* defaults except scr_allow_fg42 1, one client on the
# server. Captured 2026-09-24. The evidence is the server's own games_mp.log:
# the gametype is crates/gsc/tests/fixtures/semantics/client-probes/probe_pickup.gsc,
# which threads a waittill("touch") and a waittill("trigger") onto every watched
# item and a waittill("touch") onto every player, and logPrints one line per
# notify. The Weapon: and Item: lines are the engine's own (Touch_Item). The
# client half of the same run is mp_carentan-dm-pickup.txt beside this file.
#
# Two shells, the gsc probe first:
#   COD_LNXDED_HOME=<absolute, no '+'> SECS=150 \
#       tools/run_probe.sh client-probes/probe_pickup mp_carentan +set probe_teleport 1 +set scr_allow_fg42 1
#   cargo run -p vcod -- --net-probe 127.0.0.1:28970 --save-pickup --probe-secs 120
# scr_allow_fg42 1 is not stock: default_mp.cfg sets it 0, and
# _teams::restrictPlacedWeapons then deletes both fg42s at map load. A run
# without it has no fg42 to take.
#
# PROBE item <num> <classname> <getTime> <origin>: a watched item at first sight.
# PROBE other <num> <classname> <getTime>: any other non-player entity first
#   seen after the startup census.
# PROBE touch <num> <getTime> <otherNum>: a "touch" notify on an item.
# PROBE ptouch <playerNum> <getTime> <itemNum>: a "touch" notify on a player.
# PROBE trigger <num> <getTime> <playerNum> <swapped>: a "trigger" notify on an
#   item; <swapped> is undefined or <num>:<classname> of the weapon the pickup
#   dropped.
# PROBE teleport <playerNum> <step> <origin>: a probe_teleport move, step 1 or 2.
# Weapon: <playerNum> <weapon> and Item: <playerNum> <classname>: the engine's
#   pickup log line.
# Standing on an item logs one touch and one ptouch line per 50 ms server
# frame, while the client sent a usercmd every 16 ms: a line per frame, not
# per cmd.
